tasks.title: Admit turn and budget exhaustion as their own failure categories
tasks.objective: Give the ledger somewhere to record an invocation that never produced a candidate, so a ceiling reached is distinguishable from a candidate rejected.
acceptance_criteria: `store.py` accepts `turn_exhaustion` and `budget_exhaustion` wherever it accepts `review_rejection` and `verification_failure`, in both `record_rejection` and `retry_attempt`, and still rejects an unknown category.

A new category survives the whole path from the ledger event to the evidence a routing policy gate reads, and is then excluded there, so an invocation that produced no candidate cannot be promoted or demoted as if it had. A safelist that silently drops an unknown category before the gate sees it does not satisfy this.
Ledgers recorded before this change remain readable and their existing categories keep their meaning.
Tests cover each new category through both entry points, an unknown category still refused, and a policy gate ignoring the new categories.

tasks.title: Classify an invocation's terminal reason from its result, not its exit code
tasks.objective: Parse an agent invocation's own result before raising on the exit code, so a turn that exhausted its turns or its budget reaches the coordinator as that, rather than as a generic nonzero exit.
acceptance_criteria: The Claude adapter parses the result stream before raising on `outcome.returncode`, and a stream whose result carries `max_turns` or `budget_exhausted` raises an error carrying that classification rather than only `Claude Code execution exited with code 1`.
The Codex adapter's own terminal vocabulary is classified the same way, or its absence is recorded explicitly in the adapter rather than left implicit.
A classified terminal reason reaches the ledger as the matching failure category from the preceding ticket, so the reason is readable from saved state without re-reading raw event files.
A timeout, a malformed stream, a permission denial and an ordinary nonzero exit keep their current behavior and are not reclassified as exhaustion.
Tests drive each terminal reason through a fake agent executable and assert both the raised classification and the recorded category, never invoking a live model.

tasks.title: Enforce a dollar ceiling only where the cost basis is billed
tasks.objective: Distinguish a billed cost from a subscription list-price estimate, and stop terminating an invocation against money that was never charged.
acceptance_criteria: `telemetry.py` records the cost basis a provider reported alongside the amount, so a list-price estimate and a billed charge are distinguishable in saved state rather than sharing `provider_reported_estimate`.
A profile's `max_budget_usd` is passed to an invocation only when the resolved basis is billed; under a list basis the ceiling is not enforced and the reason is recorded rather than silently dropped.
An unknown or absent basis is treated as not billed, so a missing field cannot cause a ceiling to be enforced against an estimate.
Ledgers and invocation records written before this change remain readable, and a run with no `max_budget_usd` configured behaves exactly as it does today.
Tests cover a billed basis enforcing the ceiling, a list basis not enforcing it, an absent basis not enforcing it, and the recorded basis surviving a round trip.

tasks.title: Commit an exhausted attempt's partial tree to its own retained revision
tasks.objective: An invocation that hits a turn or budget ceiling leaves a partial tree in its worktree and nothing names it, so the work is destroyed when the worktree goes. Give that tree an immutable revision of its own, under a retained kind that is not 'candidate', so a later slice can restore it and an auditor can replay it. This ticket changes what a run records, not what it does: an exhausted run still stops exactly as it does today.
acceptance_criteria: When an invocation raises InvocationExhausted with a turn or budget category, the supervisor commits that attempt's worktree as a single commit on the attempt's base and records its revision on the attempt. An exhausted worktree with nothing changed records no revision rather than an empty commit. The commit has to happen while the run can still run Git and before the worktree is removed, which rules out the pool's cleanup path: by the time that runs the process scope is cancelled and every Git invocation raises ProcessCancelled.

That revision is not a candidate and nothing in the acceptance path may treat it as one. It carries no acceptance claims, is never verified, never reviewed, and never reaches prepare_integration. The phases a task may occupy are unchanged, and no attempt reaches the candidate phase because of it.

The revision is named by a supervisor-owned ref under a retained kind distinct from candidate and integration, and anvil retained lists and removes it on the same terms as the existing kinds, still refusing to strand a revision a ledger records.

The run's outcome is unchanged. An exhausted invocation still stops the run, with the same status, the same error, and the same failure_category slices 1 and 2 record. Only the recorded revision is new.
Ledgers and reports written before this change remain readable, and anvil retained over a run that has no exhausted revision behaves exactly as it does today.

Tests cover an exhausted worker recording the revision with the base as its single parent, an exhausted worker that changed nothing recording none, the revision surviving a prune that an ordinary gc would take, retained listing and removing it, and the run's status and failure category being unchanged by its presence. Fake agents and real temporary repositories only, never a live model.

tasks.title: Retry an exhausted attempt from its own partial tree instead of stopping the run
tasks.objective: An InvocationExhausted is still caught beside every other ProcessError and stops the whole run, so it never reaches retry: the eight exhausted invocations RUN_ECONOMICS.md measures ended sixteen runs between them. Route exhaustion into the existing retry instead, and start the replacement attempt from the revision the previous ticket recorded rather than from an empty worktree.
acceptance_criteria: A turn-exhausted or budget-exhausted invocation is a failure of that task's attempt rather than of the run: it is recorded with the failure category slice 2 defines, and the coordinator offers it the same retry a review rejection or a verification failure gets. When no retry is available the run stops exactly as it does today, with the same status and error. A budget or process failure that is not an exhaustion is unaffected. Slice 4a left the shape this has to fit: an exhausted worker thread defers cancelling the process scope, and the coordinator commits the partial tree and then cancels and raises. A retry has to be spliced in before that cancel, because every Git call raises ProcessCancelled after it, so a retry that survives the cancel cannot create a worktree or commit anything.

The replacement attempt restores the exhausted attempt's recorded revision into a worktree left at the accepted base, using the mechanism milestone 11 shipped, and is permitted to do so only while the accepted base is unchanged since the exhausted attempt began. When a peer integrated in the meantime the retry falls back to a fresh worktree. A test asserts the peer's work survives, and must be written so that it fails against a version which restores unconditionally; state in the ticket record how you confirmed it fails.

The restored revision is read from the revision the coordinator holds for the attempt in hand, which slice 4a already computes at the point the retry must happen, never from the refs/anvil/ ref that names it, because a retained ref is evidence and no retry decision may depend on one existing.

The prompt for a resumed attempt says what is true of it and nothing more: the worktree holds a partial tree a previous attempt left when it ran out of turns or budget, that tree was never reviewed and may be incomplete or internally inconsistent, and every acceptance criterion still applies and will be judged from scratch. It states no findings, because an exhausted attempt produced none.

A resumed attempt escalates to the next-ranked profile as a fresh retry does, rather than keeping its profile as an amend does. The ceiling a resumed attempt gets is the one that profile already carries; no new setting is introduced. The attempt cap is unchanged, so a resumption consumes the one retry a run has and adds none.
The replacement attempt's routing_decision records that it resumed an exhausted attempt and names the revision it restored. No new failure category is introduced.

Tests in tests/test_adaptive.py cover a resumed attempt seeing the exhausted attempt's files and going on to be accepted, the base-advanced fallback from criterion 2, an exhaustion with no retry available still stopping the run unchanged, escalation happening, and the routing_decision naming a revision that resolves. Fake agents and real temporary repositories only, never a live model.

execution.reason: Review found the change reached src/anvil/store.py and tests/test_store.py, outside criterion 1's declared sites. In scope: an exhausted attempt is 'running', never 'candidate', so the store's status gate had to admit it. The sites declaration was incomplete and is corrected here.

tasks.title: Aggregate recorded per-invocation usage into the report and the dashboard
tasks.objective: telemetry.py already parses cache creation, cache read, output and thinking tokens for every invocation, and nothing aggregates them: every number in RUN_ECONOMICS.md came from re-reading saved event streams by hand. Roll up what is already recorded so a run's cost decomposition and terminal reasons are readable without that. While the report and the ledger are open, also record which supervisor produced the run: this milestone's own measurements compare runs across days in which Anvil changed, and no saved run says which version it had.
acceptance_criteria: A run's report carries a usage aggregate over its invocations: the token components telemetry already parses, the cost with its basis kept distinct as slice 3 records it, and a breakdown by phase and terminal reason. Every value is summed from what the ledger holds; nothing is inferred, estimated, or re-derived from a raw stream.
The same aggregate is served under the existing api_version, following the change rule in docs/CLOUD_SYNC.md: adding a field or a route is permitted, and cursor ordering is not changed.
A list-price estimate is never presented as spend. Wherever a cost appears its basis appears with it, because AGENTS.md says a cost estimate is not an invoice.
A run recorded before this change, and an invocation whose usage the adapter did not report, each aggregate to what is present rather than to an error or a zero presented as a measurement.
The page shows the decomposition for a selected run and reaches the document through textContent like every other view, with numbers aligned as the existing spend table aligns them.

Tests cover the aggregate over a recorded fixture, a mixed-basis run keeping the two bases distinct, a pre-change ledger, and a missing-usage invocation, using recorded fixtures and never a live model.

A run records the version of the supervisor that produced it, in the ledger at initialization and in the report and the served run summary alongside base_sha. Today nothing does: base_sha stands in for it only because assert_clean forces the working tree to equal HEAD, which says nothing about the supervisor for a run against any repository other than Anvil's own. The ledger's user_version is bumped for the added column, and a ledger written before this change still reads, reporting the version as absent rather than failing or presenting a guess as a recorded value. Tests cover a new run recording it, a pre-change ledger reading without it, and the served summary carrying it under the existing api_version.
